newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call up on fears of loan oversubscription.
newsitem.headline: Indian call up on fears of loan oversubscription.

text.p: Indian call money rates jumped to 3.50-4.50 percent on Wednesday after opening at 0.50-0.75 percent on fears of oversubscription at a sale of state loans in the evening, dealers said.
The State Bank of India, India's largest commercial bank, was quoting 4.0 percent in latest deals.
Call rates had closed at 0.25-0.75 percent on Tuesday.
"The market is flush with funds but the fears of oversubscription at today's state loan pushed up rates," a dealer said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) sells 25 billion rupees of 13.05 percent 10-year state government bonds on April 30 and dealers expect bids to exceed the target amount.

"Most of the players have put bids far in excess of the notified amount," one dealers said. "Today the call rates are not indicative of the liquidity in the system-after knowing the amount retained by the RBI, the rate will stabilise," he said.
The securities market is expected to see a lacklusture trade on Wednesday, as the market awaits the state-loan sale.
